_comment: Provenance for schemas vendored from tinyland-inc/site.scaffold, which the
$id of every schema in this directory already names as the authority.
Recording the source revision and per-file digests is what makes the
vendoring auditable: before this file, ci-templates carried a COPY of the
v1 manifest schema with no lock and no drift gate, and it had silently
diverged from its source in BOTH directions (ci-templates gained
authorities.artifact_registry; site.scaffold gained a gitops_receiver
prohibition). Nothing compared them.
The v2 copy arrived the same way and was byte-identical at the v4.0.0
source revision. The current scaffold source removes provider and binding
state from that manifest; this release records the resulting drift without
silently changing the manifest contract alongside ActionPlan schema 3.
SCOPE IS THE WHOLE DIRECTORY, deliberately. The first draft of this record
covered the two manifest schemas only, and `just
vendored-schema-provenance-check` reported 'all 2 vendored schemas match'
over a directory holding four -- one of which, lanes.schema.json, is
load-bearing (it backs the lanes-load action that
tinyland.dev's CI runs). Coverage-shaped output enforcing less than it
reads as is the defect this whole change exists to end, so the gate now
globs schemas/*.schema.json and an unrecorded schema is an error.
STATES. `identical`: vendored bytes equal upstream bytes. `drifted`: a
known divergence, REPORTED not failed. `unsourced`: the $id names a
site.scaffold path that does not exist at source_revision, so there is
nothing to compare. Each state is asserted against the digests recorded
beside it -- an `identical` entry whose upstream_sha256 differs, or a
`drifted` entry with none, is now an error rather than unread metadata.
v1 is recorded as DRIFTED on purpose. This change does not silently adopt
upstream's v1 bytes -- that would change what every consumer is validated
against, which is a separate decision with its own review. It records the
divergence so the drift gate can report it instead of nobody noticing.
Re-vendoring recipe: copy the source file, recompute sha256 for both the
vendored copy and (for a drifted entry) the upstream one, and update
source_revision in the same change. `just vendored-schema-provenance-check`
verifies the vendored digests offline; it deliberately does NOT reach
site.scaffold, so upstream freshness -- and source_revision itself --
stay separate, advisory, non-blocking questions.
source_revision_note: Exact signed site.scaffold #163 ActionPlan/v4 schema-3 source commit. This provenance records source identity only; it does not authorize a ci-templates release, site adoption, provider rollout, or runtime proof.

files.state_note: Known divergence, reported not reconciled. Current site.scaffold v4 removes provider selection and binding-state fields from the consumer manifest; changing the released manifest validator is a separate migration from the ActionPlan schema-3 co-move.
The legacy v1 source was deleted from site.scaffold before this source revision. The vendored copy remains only for existing manifest routing; retiring it is a separate compatibility decision.

The $id names tinyland-inc/site.scaffold docs/schemas/blahaj-dispatch.schema.json, which returns 404 at source_revision (probed 2026-08-29). There is no upstream file to digest, so no drift claim is possible in either direction. Recorded rather than excluded because '$id names the authority' is the heuristic the rest of this file rests on, and here it is demonstrably unreliable -- that is a finding to keep visible, not a file to leave unpinned.
